definition: A region of space in which an electric charge experiences an electric force.
The electric force per unit charge on a small positive test charge at a point, $E = \frac{F}{q}$; a vector, measured in $\text{N C}^{-1}$ or $\text{V m}^{-1}$.
An imagined small positive charge placed at a point to measure the field there, small enough not to disturb the charges that make the field.

A line showing the direction of the force on a positive charge at each point; lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges (or at infinity), never cross, and are closer together where the field is stronger.
An electric field with the same strength and direction at every point, drawn as parallel, equally spaced lines; between parallel plates its strength is $E = \frac{V}{d}$.
A region in which a magnet, a magnetic material, or a moving charge or current experiences a force.
A line showing the direction of the force on a north pole at each point; outside a magnet the lines run from north to south, and they always form closed loops.
